page_title: Dantrolene — you're home. it locks anyway.

summary.name: Dantrolene
summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that stops the screen from locking while connected to a chosen home Wi-Fi network, with normal locking resuming on other networks.
use_cases: Keep a Mac unlocked while working at home
Stop screen locking on a trusted home network only
Keep a Mac awake with the lid closed on home Wi-Fi
Avoid password prompts on a personal desk setup
Let presentations or Zoom calls keep the display on
summary.what_it_does: Dantrolene lets you pick a home Wi-Fi network from the menu bar. In automatic mode it prevents screen locking on that network and restores normal locking on other networks. It has three modes: automatic, always on, and off. The display still dims and goes dark after the usual idle time, and moving the mouse or keyboard returns it without a password. It yields when Zoom, a presentation, or another app holds a display assertion. It stores the network name locally, makes no network requests, and can launch at login.
notable: Wi-Fi network name determines when screen locking is suppressed
Works with the companion app Adrafinil to keep a lid-closed Mac awake on the home network
Open source under MIT license, makes no network requests
Uses private frameworks for display dimming, which may break after macOS updates
caveats: Requires Location Services permission to read Wi-Fi names, though it uses only the network name
Wi-Fi name is not a security check; another hotspot with the same name can trigger it
Display dimming relies on private frameworks and may break after a macOS update
